title: など — “and so on / things like ～”
summary: など follows one or more examples and shows that there are other similar things too. It is often used as 「A や B など」, and it can also soften what you say by treating the item as just one example.

patterns.form: 名詞A ＋ や ＋ 名詞B ＋ など
patterns.gloss: りんごやみかんなどの果物 (fruit such as apples and oranges)

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ など ＋ を／が／に…
patterns.gloss: 掃除や洗濯などをします (do cleaning, laundry, and so on)

body.p: など is a particle for giving examples. Link several items with や and put など at the end. You can follow it with の to modify a noun (などの果物) or with particles such as を and が.
Use it to give examples while signaling that there are more: 休みの日は掃除や洗濯などをします, かばんの中に本やノートなどが入っている. In casual speech, とか is also used.
など signals that the list is not complete. To list everything, use と. With a single item, as in お茶など、いかがですか, it becomes a modest, polite offer.

examples.ja: りんごやみかんなどの果物（くだもの）が好（す）きです。
examples.romaji: Ringo ya mikan nado no kudamono ga suki desu.
examples.tr: I like fruit such as apples and oranges.

examples.ja: 休（やす）みの日（ひ）は掃除（そうじ）や洗濯（せんたく）などをします。
examples.romaji: Yasumi no hi wa sōji ya sentaku nado o shimasu.
examples.tr: On days off, I do cleaning, laundry, and so on.

examples.ja: かばんの中（なか）に本（ほん）やノートなどが入（はい）っている。
examples.romaji: Kaban no naka ni hon ya nōto nado ga haitte iru.
examples.tr: There are books, notebooks, and so on in my bag.

pitfalls: To list everything, use と. ～や～など implies there are more.
Do not drop the particle after など: 掃除や洗濯などします is unnatural; say などをします.
